source.note: Legacy Organic Chemistry I cards converted into ochem pipeline source records without changing the original question or answer meaning.

cards.front: What suffix indicates a carboxylic acid?
cards.back: `-oic acid`.
visual_requirements: assets/organic/carboxylic-acid.svg
cards.merge_notes: Near existing Chapter 3 functional-group inventory where carboxylic acid has name ending -oic acid; keep as legacy suffix recall.

cards.front: What suffix indicates an ester?
cards.back: `-oate`.
visual_requirements: assets/organic/ester.svg
cards.merge_notes: Near existing Chapter 3 functional-group inventory where ester has name ending -oate; keep as legacy suffix recall.

cards.front: What suffix indicates an amide?
cards.back: `-amide`.
visual_requirements: assets/organic/amide.svg
cards.merge_notes: Near existing Chapter 3 functional-group inventory where amide has name ending -amide; keep as legacy suffix recall.

cards.front: What suffix indicates an amine?
cards.back: `-amine`.
visual_requirements: assets/organic/amine.svg
cards.merge_notes: Near existing Chapter 3 functional-group inventory where amine has name ending -amine; keep as legacy suffix recall.

cards.front: What suffix indicates a nitrile?
cards.back: `-nitrile`.
visual_requirements: assets/organic/nitrile.svg
cards.merge_notes: Near existing Chapter 3 functional-group inventory where nitrile has name ending -nitrile; keep as legacy suffix recall.

cards.front: What suffix indicates a thiol?
cards.back: `-thiol`.
visual_requirements: assets/organic/thiol.svg
cards.merge_notes: Near existing Chapter 3 functional-group inventory where thiol has name ending -thiol; keep as legacy suffix recall.

cards.front: What does `di-` mean in a name?
cards.back: Two of the named group or substituent.
visual_requirements: Show two identical substituents or functional groups on one parent scaffold.
cards.merge_notes: Overlaps with existing Chapter 3 naming guidance that uses di-, tri-, and tetra- for repeated identical substituents; keep as standalone legacy multiplier recall.

cards.front: What does `tri-` mean in a name?
cards.back: Three of the named group or substituent.
visual_requirements: Show three identical substituents or functional groups on one parent scaffold.
cards.merge_notes: Overlaps with existing Chapter 3 naming guidance that uses di-, tri-, and tetra- for repeated identical substituents; keep as standalone legacy multiplier recall.

cards.front: What does `tetra-` mean in a name?
cards.back: Four of the named group or substituent.
visual_requirements: Show four identical substituents or functional groups on one parent scaffold.
cards.merge_notes: Overlaps with existing Chapter 3 naming guidance that uses di-, tri-, and tetra- for repeated identical substituents; keep as standalone legacy multiplier recall.

cards.front: What does `diene` mean?
cards.back: A molecule with two carbon-carbon double bonds.
visual_requirements: Show a carbon skeleton with two C=C bonds highlighted.
cards.merge_notes: Related to alkene suffix cards and Chapter 3 functional-group inventory; no exact diene-only card found.

cards.front: What does `yne` tell you about bonding?
cards.back: There is a carbon-carbon triple bond.
visual_requirements: assets/organic/alkyne.svg
cards.merge_notes: Near-duplicate of legacy-organic-chemistry-i-017, which asks for the suffix indicating an alkyne; this card preserves the reverse bonding cue.

cards.front: What does `ene` tell you about bonding?
cards.back: There is a carbon-carbon double bond.
visual_requirements: assets/organic/alkene.svg
cards.merge_notes: Near-duplicate of legacy-organic-chemistry-i-016, which asks for the suffix indicating an alkene; this card preserves the reverse bonding cue.

cards.front: What is the parent chain?
cards.back: The main carbon chain chosen as the base of the name.
visual_requirements: Show a branched alkane with the selected parent chain highlighted.
cards.merge_notes: Overlaps with existing Chapter 3 parent-chain selection and naming workflow cards; keep as a concise legacy definition.

cards.front: What is a substituent?
cards.back: A branch or group attached to the parent chain.
visual_requirements: Show a parent chain with a branch or attached group highlighted as the substituent.
cards.merge_notes: Overlaps with existing Chapter 3 alkyl-group and substituent naming coverage; keep as a concise legacy definition.

cards.front: What does a number/locant do in a name?
cards.back: It tells where a substituent, multiple bond, or functional group is located.
visual_requirements: Show a numbered parent chain with a substituent, multiple bond, or functional group position called out.
cards.merge_notes: Overlaps with existing Chapter 3 and Chapter 4 lowest-locant rules; keep as a general locant-purpose card.

cards.front: What is the first major step in naming a simple organic molecule?
cards.back: Find the parent chain containing the highest-priority functional group or multiple bond.
visual_requirements: Show candidate parent chains and highlight the selected chain containing the highest-priority functional group or multiple bond.
cards.merge_notes: Overlaps with existing Chapter 3 naming workflow; keep because it includes the functional-group or multiple-bond containment cue.

cards.front: What do you do after finding the parent chain?
cards.back: Number the chain to give important groups and multiple bonds the lowest reasonable numbers.
visual_requirements: Show a parent chain numbered from the better end so important groups and multiple bonds receive lower locants.
cards.merge_notes: Overlaps with existing Chapter 3 and Chapter 4 lowest-locant rules; keep as the next-step workflow card.

cards.front: How are substituents listed in a name?
cards.back: Usually alphabetically, with locants showing their positions.
visual_requirements: Show two or more substituents with locants and an alphabetical ordering cue.
cards.merge_notes: Overlaps with existing Chapter 3 alkane naming rules and Chapter 4 alphabetical tie-break cards; keep as a general substituent-listing cue.

cards.front: Do `di-`, `tri-`, and `tetra-` count for alphabetizing substituents?
cards.back: Usually no; alphabetize by the substituent name itself.
visual_requirements: Show repeated substituents in a name and mark that multiplier prefixes are ignored for alphabetizing.
cards.merge_notes: Near-duplicate of existing Chapter 3 rule to ignore multiplier prefixes when alphabetizing and Chapter 4 alphabetical tie-break details; keep as a standalone legacy rule.

cards.front: What does `N-` mean in names like `N-methylacetamide`?
cards.back: The substituent is attached to nitrogen.
visual_requirements: Show an amide with a methyl substituent attached to nitrogen and the N locant highlighted.
cards.merge_notes: Related to amide functional-group cards but not an exact duplicate; keep to preserve the heteroatom-locant naming rule.
